chapter: Papa Celestin and the fiesta bands
title: Getting Congo Square and the first concert with Papa Celestin and Lizzie Miles
summary: Mrs. Synigal tells how she won use of Congo Square from the city, and how Celestin's band and Lizzie Miles reconciled at the first concert.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I'd like to ask you about that very first year. What kind of music did you have when you said it was in Congo Square with some people called Borrigan?

What kind of music we had? We had Papa Salastare himself with Lizzie Miles singing. We had the best. The people start from the bottom up, but we had the best first. We had the best first. We've never had a concert like that since. But he donated his time. Well, I tell you how we got this Beauregard Square. Congo Square. I will call it Congo Square because I knew it by Congo Square. The Pops concert was going on. You know about the Pops concert. And so I went to see the mayor to ask for this square. And he was very busy at the time. And he told me to call up the scero, his assistant. Say, make an appointment with him. And he's very nice. He'll do just as I do. So I phoned him and made an appointment. And so when I got there, I said, what can I do for you, Mrs. Senegal? I said, oh, the sky's the limit. He said, I said, the sky's the limit. He said, well, that's all right. That's all right. We'll bring it down. I said, you just don't know what I came to ask you for. So he said, well, have a seat. Let's go. He said, well, go on, shoot. So I said, well, I came to ask you for Congo Square. He says, Congo Square? Where? What is Congo Square? I say, Congo Square? You don't know what is Congo Square? He says, no. He says, Washington Square, Lafayette Square, all the squares. He was named. I said, no, no. Well, where is Congo Square? I say, you're Lafayette Square, right in front of your municipal auditorium. A very large square. A very large square. A very large square. Right opposite your auditorium. He says, no, really? I says, yes, it is. I said, that's Congo Square. So he says, well, I never knew that before. I says, well, how do you know? He asked me how did I know that. I say, I was told that from my grandparents. And I know it's so because I have some people living today who told me that's where Marie Laveau used to do her dances on Sunday afternoon. And he says, that time, that time. I said, yes, I know what I'm talking about. It's not in the books. And I say, I know so well it's not in the books. Because I'm telling you something that it's not in the books that I know. So he says, well, if you know that much about Congo Square, what else you want? What else you got to tell me that I don't know of? I was, so he said, I said, well, now you have your pop concert going on now. Well, I'd like to have Congo Square Vow concert for the Fiestas, Creole Fiestas concert. He says, when? I says, well, we haven't set an exact date yet. He says, wait, let me tell. Well, I can help you. Wait a minute. He says, well, you know the pop concert is going on now. I said, yes. He says, well, if you can get your concert to come on immediately after the pops finishes, I will ask the head ones to leave all the lights, all the equipment, just as is for you to have your one night after. So I said, oh, that's fine. He said, but you have to go in. I'll ring them up. But you'll have to go yourself. I said, I'll go anywhere. Just send me. Just send me. So he sent me to the club on Rampart Street. The Y, Y MC on Rampart Street. Sent me there to Mr. Poche. I remember. That's his name. He told me to go see him because he was the chairman of that pop concert at that time. And asked him would he and his company or his associate would let me have the club on the day after they finished. So he told me he would call his men together. And lo and behold, he called me and said, yes, we could have it with everything as it stood. Everything. The loudspeaker and everything just as it stood. And no charges. With all the fence up and all the stage, the piano, everything just as it was. As long as we use it that night, we have to make our date the night after so it wouldn't stay so long. And he said, of course, they have to pay the man who will take care of it. You know, the, what do you call it? Night watchman. He said, now we can only pay one night for it. That's the night we are closing. So if you don't come on the night afterwards, they will close you down because we cannot pay for that night watchman. I said, we'll be there. Don't worry. We'll be there. So now, then I, I, we got it together and had our tickets and everything and we went on that night. Now we didn't, we didn't dance that quadrille that first night. We danced it the second year. The first year we didn't dance it for the first year. We had Papa Celisna. Well, I called him and I asked him, I said, what can you do for his Papa Celisna? He says, well, I'm telling you, if the city is so good to you and going to give you all that, I'm giving you my, my band for nothing. Now I'm coming out there with my band. And I phoned Lizzie Miles and she said, oh, well, you know, I should say this now. Papa Celisna said, she don't fool somebody else. She said, but I'll be there. I'll be there. I don't know. He didn't play much for her. I don't think something like that. But she says, I'll be there. And do you know they made friends that night? Papa Celisna said, Lizzie Miles made friends that night because she was playing for, Al Marico was playing for her, you know? Yeah. And so, well, he told me why. She didn't think he could play for her as some kind of, I said, well, as long as you admire, I don't care what you all do between you, but just be there and play for us, for our fiestas. So they did. And Papa Celisna began playing, what's her famous song? Billy? Bill Bailey. Bill Bailey.
Bill Bailey, once the piece come over.

They forgot whatever they had. Whatever they had, they forgot. Here was Lizzie Miles, Bill Bailey, and Papa Celisna, he said, now you know Miss Senegal, took you to bring us back together again. And they really, really did put it on that night. We really had a wonderful concert. That was the beginning of our fiesta, right there. And it was all given to us. Given to us. All given to us. From the city on down. And Mayor Maestrie, he sent word and he told me, anything we needed, we could have. Any city equipment that we needed, we could have. And so far, we've been having it. And we had a concert, as you spoke of, on Columbus Street.
